papers.title_in_file: Single-Pixel Pattern Recognition with Coherent Nonlinear Optics
papers.version_note: arXiv:2010.02273v1 preprint of the Optics Letters letter, compiled October 7, 2020.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental letter combining mode-selective sum-frequency image conversion with 40 Laguerre-Gaussian pump modes and a deep neural network to classify MNIST digits, with and without added phase noise.

assertions.value: The authors state that a mode-lock laser generates optical pulses of about 300 fs FWHM at 50 MHz repetition rate, and that two inline narrowband WDMs select a 1558 nm pump and a 1545 nm signal; the pump and signal are expanded to beam waists of 2.8 mm and 2.6 mm.
quotes: A mode-lock laser generates optical pulses with ∼300 fs full width at half maximum (FWHM) and 50 MHz repetition rate.
one at 1558 nm as the pump and the other at 1545 nm as the signal
expanded to a 2.8-mm beam waist (FWHM) for the pump and 2.6 mm for the signal
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SLMs are Santec SLM-100 with a pixel pitch of about 10.4 x 10.4 um and an active area of about 1.4 x 1 cm, and that the digit images are uploaded onto SLM1 as phase mask patterns.
quotes: The SLMs are Santec SLM-100 and have the same specs: pixel pitch ∼ 10.4 × 10.4 µm, active area ∼ 1.4 × 1 cm.
the MNIST digit images are uploaded onto SLM1 as phase mask patterns.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the nonlinear crystal is a temperature-stabilized PPLN (poling period 19.36 um, total length 1 cm, 5 mol.% MgO doped), with a normalized conversion efficiency of about 1%/W/cm assuming optimal focusing, and that the sum-frequency light is at 775.5 nm.

assertions.value: The authors define mode-selective image conversion (MSIC) as frequency conversion driven by a spatially structured pump beam in a nonlinear crystal, so that only a single signal mode of prescribed phase coherence is converted efficiently.
quotes: MSIC is implemented by applying a spatially structured pump beam to drive the frequency conversion in a nonlinear crystal
only a single signal mode of certain prescribed phase coherence can be converted e
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines MSIC at its first use.

assertions.value: The authors state that each input image is processed by MSIC through frequency upconversion by pump beams in 40 different Laguerre-Gaussian modes, and that for each mode the converted power is measured and used as the input to the DNN.
quotes: through frequency upconversion by pump beams in 40 different Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes.
For each mode, the converted power is measured and used as the input to the DNN for subsequent machine learning.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of its architecture.

assertions.value: The authors state that they simulated 110 LG modes with l in [-5, 5] and p in [0, 9], then chose the 40 most effective modes with l in [-2, 2] and p in [0, 7] as the experimental pump modes, based on simulated classification accuracy.
quotes: start from simulating the performance with 110 LG modes with
l ∈ [−5, 5] and p ∈ [0, 9], as the SF generation e
we choose a subset of most effective 40 modes with l ∈ [−2, 2] and p ∈ [0, 7] as the pump modes for our experiments.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The 40 modes are the 5 values of l times the 8 values of p; the selection used simulated accuracy, so the subset was tuned on simulation before the experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the DNN has one convolutional layer with 16 filters and kernel size 2, five fully connected layers of 512, 256, 128, 64 and 32 units, and an output layer of 10 neurons for the 10 classes.
quotes: and one output layer with 10 neurons for the 10 different classes
There are 16

have 512, 256, 128, 64, and 32 units, respectively.

assertions.value: The authors state that the benchmark dataset is the first 600 handwritten images of each digit of MNIST, resized from 28x28 to 400x400 pixels, and split after shuffling into 4800 training images and 1200 testing images.
quotes: 600 handwritten images of each digit in the MNIST database as our dataset
from 28×28 to 400×400 pixels to match with the SLM pitch and signal beam diameter
training (4800 images) and testing sets (1200 images)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the dataset it evaluates on.
assertions.reader_inference: Only a 6000-image subset of MNIST and one train/test split are used, so the reported accuracies are not full-MNIST results.

assertions.value: The authors state that, using the training set, the power readings for each LG mode are normalized across all digits so that the features contribute about equally, and that the 40 normalized readings per image are mapped onto a 4x10 matrix for the DNN, trained on an NVIDIA Quadro T2000 GPU.
quotes: the power readings are normalized across all digits so that different features extracted by those modes contribute more or less equally to the machine learning.
the 40 normalized readings for each image are mapped onto a 4×10 matrix for feeding into the DNN for training on a NVIDIA Quadro T2000 graphics processing unit (GPU).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report a simulated recognition accuracy of 100% for the training set and 99.83% for the testing set, with accuracy converging stably over epochs.
quotes: the recognition accuracy of 100% is achieved for the training and 99.83% for the testing dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that two data collection procedures were used: a sequential run, measuring the 600 images of each digit as a group before the next digit, and a loop run, measuring groups of 10 containing one image per digit.
quotes: where the 600 images for each digit are measured in a group before moving to the next digit.
The second runs in a loop, with the images measured in groups of 10, with each containing one image for every digit.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report an experimental accuracy of 99.49% for the sequential run on the original MNIST subset, which they compare with the 99.83% simulated value.
quotes: The sequential run reaches an accuracy score of 99.49%, which approaches to the theoretical
value of 99.83% obtained in our simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The 'theoretical' 99.83% is the simulated test accuracy, not an analytic bound.

assertions.value: The authors report an experimental accuracy of 94.25% for the loop run on the original MNIST subset, and attribute the drop to experimental instabilities and noise during the elongated data taking.
quotes: With the loop run, on the other hand, the accuracy is dropped to 94.25%.
This may be caused by the experimental instabilities and noise during the elongated data taking
assertions.reader_inference: The cause is the authors' conjecture; no test of it is reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that the added noise is a phase mask of 10x10-pixel clusters with random phases uniformly distributed over [0, 2pi), covering 40% of the pixels.
quotes: Each noise spot in the noise mask is in a cluster with 10×10 pixels
The noise cluster each have random phase values uniformly distributed between [0, 2π), and together they take up 40% of the total pixels.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors define SNR in decibels as ten times the base-10 logarithm of the ratio of the phase variance of a digit image to the phase variance of the noise mask.
quotes: SNR = 10 × log10(σs2/σn2),
where σs2 and σn2 are the phase variance of a digit image and noise mask, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its SNR measure.

assertions.value: The authors report that the SNR in the experiment varies between -19.2 dB and -5.3 dB, with a mean of -11.2 dB.
quotes: current experiment varies between -19.2 dB and -5.3 dB, with a
mean value -11.2 dB.

assertions.value: The authors report an accuracy of 95.32% for the sequential run on noise-added images, with the low-accuracy entries located near the diagonal of the confusion matrix.
quotes: accuracy reaches 95.32%
images are prone to be mis-classi
assertions.reader_inference: The authors read the near-diagonal errors as confusion among neighboring digits.

assertions.value: The authors report an accuracy of only 79.05% for the loop run on noise-added images, a larger drop than in the noise-free case.
quotes: the recognition accuracy is only 79.05% in the loop run case
marking an enlarged drop than the non-noise case as in Fig. 3.

assertions.value: The authors state that the system speed is limited by the SLM response time of about 0.5 s, that a pause of 1.5 s is set per mask, and that measuring all MNIST images therefore takes days.
quotes: the overall system speed is limited by the SLM response time (∼ 0.5 s)
a pause time of 1.5 s is set in the experiments to ensure a well uploaded mask
Therefore, it takes days to measure all MNIST images.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit themselves.

assertions.value: The authors state that the system is stable over short times but that beam drifts and ambient noise in the table-top free-space setup cause measurement errors that reduce recognition accuracy over days.
quotes: While the system is stable during short time
beam drifts, and ambient noise in our table-top settings over free space.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit themselves.

assertions.value: The authors claim that MSIC reduces a large amount of pixel-wise information to only 40 signatures.
quotes: It reduces a large amount of pixel-wise information to only 40 signatures
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no comparison with a DNN on raw pixels, so the benefit of the reduction is not measured.

assertions.value: The authors claim that, unlike linear optical approaches, MSIC involves no direct modulation on the signal, eliminating the otherwise inevitable modulation loss or noise.
quotes: Unlike linear optical approaches, MSIC does not involve any direct modulation on the signal, thus eliminating the otherwise inevitable modulation loss or noise
assertions.reader_inference: The paper cites its reference 38 for this and reports no loss measurement.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the nonlinear optics step uses all-to-all connection and speed-of-light processing of large-volume image data, which are overwhelming for typical electronic digital processors.
quotes: The nonlinear optics step utilizes all-to-all connection and speed-of-light processing of large-volume image data
assertions.reader_inference: The measured system is slow (days of data taking), so this speed claim is prospective and not demonstrated.

assertions.value: The authors state a hope to replace the SLMs with micro-mirror devices, where orders of magnitude speedup is expected, and to address free-space fluctuations and ambient noise with an enclosed design.
quotes: we hope to replace the current SLMs with much higher speed devices such as those of micro-mirrors, where orders of magnitude speedup is expected.
which shall be addressed by an improved, enclosed design.
